task: Bilirubin metabolism & jaundice cert: heme -> (heme oxygenase) biliverdin -> (biliverdin reductase) unconjugated bilirubin (lipophilic, albumin-bound, not renally excreted) -> hepatic uptake -> UGT1A1 glucuronidation -> conjugated bilirubin (water-soluble, renally excretable) -> bile -> gut -> urobilinogen/stercobilin. Required falsifier: reproduce the unconjugated-vs-conjugated diagnostic split (pre-hepatic/hemolysis + Gilbert/Crigler-Najjar = unconjugated; obstructive/hepatocellular = conjugated) against a 'single bilirubin pool' adversary. Dysfunction: neonatal jaundice (immature UGT1A1 + high RBC turnover + enterohepatic recycling), phototherapy photoisomerization mechanism, kernicterus (unconjugated bilirubin crosses immature BBB), Gilbert vs Crigler-Najjar genetics, biliary obstruction.

Standard small-molecule/protein-chemistry-stoichiometry tier for the Hb/heme/bilirubin molecular-weight constants (bilirubin MW derived transparently from its C33H36N4O6 atomic formula in the script, not hardcoded from memory; Hb-tetramer constants reused VERBATIM from the sibling scripts/msk/iron_hepcidin.py for cross-doc consistency, re-verified by bonus gate G0). overall_verdict.f6_kernicterus_fixed_threshold_adversary: PASS -- a 'single eternal bilirubin number' adversary is forced against two independent, decorrelated facts that must BOTH hold: (a) Bhutani 1999's own hour-specific nomogram shows a high-risk-zone likelihood ratio of 14.08 vs. a low-risk-zone likelihood ratio of 0 at the SAME chronological-age window -- a fixed single-number rule cannot reproduce hour-of-life-dependent risk-zone discrimination by construction; (b) the AAP guideline's own numeric thresholds factually CHANGED between 2004 and 2022, with the 2022 technical report's own quoted words citing new neurotoxicity evidence as the reason. Both hold; the adversary falls; kernicterus risk is multifactorial/risk-stratified, not a single sharp step function.
